analysis.title: Upwork Inc. (UPWK) Q3'26 Review: Continued Progress on Enterprise and AI-Native Demand Channels Amid Marketplace Headwinds
key_insights: Upwork's Q3'26 revenue and Adj. EBITDA came in above the high end of company guidance. GS attributes this to higher-value customer activity and cost discipline.
Active Clients fell 10% YoY to 717K, below GS (739K) and consensus (760K). GS cites AI automation, a focus on quality over volume, lower-value work leaving the platform, and changing search behavior.

Enterprise progress: accelerated migrations onto Lifted, three new enterprise customer wins, and the acquisition of WorkMotion to expand global employer-of-record capabilities. Management now expects Lifted GSV to grow more than 30% in FY26.
Enterprise revenue of $26mm missed GS ($30mm) and consensus ($27mm) because customers are still moving from the legacy business to Lifted.
Business Plus GSV grew 132% YoY and is now 8% of total GSV. Business Plus active clients grew 154% YoY.
GSV from freelancers with AI skills rose 55% YoY to $112mm in Q3, an annualized run-rate near $450mm.
The MCP server generates more than $3mm of annualized Connects revenue, and weekly active users are up 20x since launch. Upwork Now was newly launched to place Upwork inside AI workflows.

Management raised FY26 Adj. EBITDA guidance but guided Q4 revenue and Adj. EBITDA below GS and Street. It also flagged a sequential margin step-down into Q4 and FY27 from marketing spend, WorkMotion integration costs, and mix shift as Lifted scales.

GS cut 2027 estimates sharply: GSV $3.40bn (from $3.79bn), Adj. EBITDA $194mm (from $231mm), Adj. EPS $1.13 (from $1.39), and active clients 604K (from 704K). FY26 Adj. EBITDA and Adj. EPS were raised to $237.9mm and $1.48.

GS reiterates Buy and raises the 12-month price target to $13.00 from $11.50, implying 33.7% upside from $9.72. The valuation uses 7.0x EV/GAAP EBITDA (unchanged) and 10.0x EV/FCF-SBC (from 8.0x), blended equally.
GS expects investor focus to stay on the balance between core marketplace pressure and how fast Enterprise, Business Plus, AI-skilled work and AI demand channels contribute to growth.

market_movers.rationale: Buy reiterated and PT raised from $11.50 on updated estimates after Q3. GS sees Upwork positively levered to a large and growing TAM despite marketplace pressure.

earnings_insights: Q3'26 reported (company data): revenue $186mm vs GS est $179mm and consensus $180mm, guidance was $176-184mm. Take rate 20.3%.
Q3'26 reported: Adj. EBITDA $64mm (34.4% margin) vs GS est $52mm and consensus $52mm, guidance was $50-54mm. Adj. EPS $0.40 vs consensus $0.32. GAAP EPS $0.25 vs consensus $0.16.
Q3'26 reported: GSV $914mm vs consensus $895mm. Active Clients 717K vs consensus 760K. GSV per active client $5,418 vs consensus $5,101. Marketplace revenue $159mm vs consensus $153mm.

GS estimates (not reported) for Q4'26: GSV $0.89bn (from $0.90bn), revenue $174mm (from $177mm), Adj. EBITDA $53mm (from $54mm), GAAP EPS $0.23 (unchanged). Q4 revenue and Adj. EBITDA guidance is below GS and Street.
GS estimates for FY27: GSV $3.40bn (from $3.79bn), revenue $678mm (from $754mm), Adj. EBITDA $194mm (from $231mm), GAAP EPS $0.81 (from $0.95). These are forecasts.
GS estimates for FY26: revenue $747mm (from $743mm), Adj. EBITDA $237.9mm (from $226.9mm), Adj. EPS $1.48 (from $1.32), GAAP EPS $0.91 (from $0.84). These are forecasts.
risk_factors: Potential to lose market share to competitors.
Broader adoption of freelancing and the shift online may occur slower than modeled.
Slower adoption of managed services could mean lower take rates than modeled.
Exposure to global macro volatility, including exposure to Russia/Ukraine, and to investor risk appetite for growth stocks.
Continued decline in active clients from AI automation, the quality-over-volume strategy and evolving search behavior.
Margin step-down in Q4 and FY27 from WorkMotion integration, incremental marketing spend and Lifted mix shift.

tension_points.bull_case: Enterprise (Lifted), Business Plus (GSV +132% YoY) and AI-skilled work (GSV +55% YoY) are growing, and AI channels such as the MCP server are adding revenue. Q3 revenue and Adj. EBITDA beat guidance, and FY26 Adj. EBITDA guidance was raised.
tension_points.bear_case: Active Clients fell 10% YoY and missed estimates. Enterprise revenue missed during the Lifted migration, and Q4 revenue and EBITDA were guided below Street with margins stepping down into FY27. GS cut 2027 revenue to $678mm from $754mm.
